To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystal structure of a Baeyer–Viller monooxygenase (BVMO), 3,6-Diketocamphae monooxygenase, was solved and that the FMN cofactor is oriented differently compared with other luciferase family enzymes, which may be related to the different catalytic properties of this BVMO.
the oxygenating constituent of the 3,6-DKM monooxygenase is an iron–sulfur cluster, and that the FMN cofactor is bound in a different orientation compared with the other luciferase-family proteins.

the oxygenation of camphor by the 3,6-DKO enzyme proceeds via a Baeyer–Villard oxidation, and that the crystal structure of 3,60-diketocarnphene monooxygenase is the first crystal structure for a type II Baeyervilliger monooxgenase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel Baeyer–Viliger reactions, the development of new catalysts and the mechanistic understanding of Baeyer–Viligier reactions.
the development of a new class of Baeyer–Villerger monooxygenase (BVMO)-based biocatalysts for asymmetric synthesis and biotransformations.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of Baeyer-Villiger oxidation reactions catalyzed by flavin-dependent monooxygenases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structure of 3, 6-diketopentanoic acid monooxygenase is an example of a new class of Baeyer–Villardge monooxygenase that has a new type of FMN binding site.
the Baeyer–Viliger reaction is a reaction of oxidation of ketones by molecular oxygen to give lactones and the oxidation of aldehydes to acids.

the oxygenase activity of the Baeyer–Villerger monooxygenase is a two step process, in the first step a hydroperoxide is formed by an oxygenation reaction of the substrate by the flavin cofactor, and in the second step the hydroperoxide is converted to the lactone by a Baeyer–Villegr oxidation reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first crystal structure for a type II Baeyers-Villiger monooxigenase and that it reveals a different ring conformation of the FMN cofactor.
we have identified a new class of Baeyer–Villardgeases that are related to bacterial luciferases and that the Baeyer–Viliger monooxygenases are a new family of enzymes with a common fold.
the crystal structures of the oxygenase component of a type II BVM, 3,6-DKM, were solved and the mechanism was investigated by using the structural and kinetic data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have solved the crystal structure of a Baeyer–Villerger monooxygenase (BVMO) that catalyses the conversion of a bicyclic ketone (3,6-dihydro-6-methyl-2H-pyran-2-one) to a monocyclic lactone (4-hydroxy-2-methyl-2(5H)-furanone) in a reaction that involves Baeyer–Viliger oxidation of the bicyclic ketones.
this enzyme is a very good example of a Baeyer–Viliger monooxygenases (BVMOs) that are used for biocatalysis.
the oxygenation mechanism of Baeyer–Villerger monooxygenases is different from that of flavin-dependent monooxygenases and cytochrome P450s.
